name: Casey Barner
strengths: Barner stays in-phase in man coverage and shadows receivers through the route with polished feet.
Barner flips his hips cleanly out of the backpedal and runs verticals stride-for-stride.
Barner closes late and contests — diving PBU / ball disruption when slightly out of phase.
Barner shows compact safety build that wins with polish and quickness more than length — camp and Friday-night temperament as a playmaker.
weaknesses: Barner still needs mass to take on bigger SEC slot TEs and sustain box collisions every down.
comparison: Barner comps to Antoine Winfield Jr. — 5-9 / ~203 mold, compact coverage safety who wins with polish, man-match feet, and late ball disruption (size-matched within ~1–2" of Barner's 5-10.5 / 190 frame).
projection: Barner projects as develop into the secondary, earn early nickel and special-teams snaps, then compete for a starting safety job — starter upside as a coverage-first FS/nickel safety.
schemeFit: Barner fits as a coverage-first safety who can match in the slot and play single-high or split-field with polish.
insiderNotes: Barner stays in-phase in man, flips hips cleanly out of the backpedal, and runs verticals stride-for-stride. Closes late to contest and disrupt the ball — compact build that wins with polish and quickness more than length.
